Definition: from G1475; to raze:--lay even with the ground.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus uses this word once, in His warning over Jerusalem, saying her enemies will lay her even with the ground and not leave one stone upon another. It is a word of total levelling, a city brought down flat because she did not know the time of her visitation.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus wept over Jerusalem because He knew what was coming, and His warning still calls every city and every heart to recognise Him while there is time.
